reason: E2 supports that heterogeneous lattice strain causes unusual dislocation behaviors (multiple kinks/jogs, bidirectional cross slips) and strength-ductility synergy, directly backing the first premise. E1 supports that nano-twinning is an important additional deformation mode enhancing toughness in CrCoNi, partially supporting the first premise. However, no cited evidence supports the claims about chemical short-range order impeding mechanisms, causing toughness loss, or the effect of Pd addition, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: Heterogeneous lattice strains enable multiple energy-dissipating deformation mechanisms (multiple dislocation cross slips, nano-twinning) in single-phase HEAs.
Uniformly distributed lattice distortions promote favorable dislocation activity and crack-tip shielding, retaining toughness.
Chemical short-range order or phase segregation locally impedes these deformation mechanisms.
Impeded deformation mechanisms due to chemical inhomogeneities lead to premature crack propagation and toughness loss.
A homogenizing heat treatment with minor Pd addition can enhance chemical homogenization and modify lattice strain distribution to improve toughness.
